question: _________ has a curving shape, a feature found in Nagara architecture.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shikhara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Shikhara** is a characteristic feature of Nagara architecture, commonly seen in North Indian temples.
 
• It has a **curving shape**, often likened to a mountain peak, which is why it is named 'Shikhara' (meaning 'mountain peak' in Sanskrit).
 
• The Shikhara is the **tallest part of the temple** and is usually situated directly above the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha) where the main deity resides.
 
• This architectural element is designed to be **visually striking** and is often elaborately decorated with intricate carvings and sculptures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antarala**

 
 
• The Antarala is a small antechamber or foyer between the garbhagriha (sanctum) and the mandapa (hall).
 
• It serves as a transitional space in the temple architecture and is typically found in larger temples.
 
 
 
• **Mandapa**
 
 
• The Mandapa is a pillared hall or pavilion for public rituals and ceremonies, often situated in front of the main temple.
 
• It is used by devotees to assemble, pray, and perform various rituals.
 
 
 
• **Kutina**
 
 
• Kutina is a less commonly referenced term in temple architecture but can refer to small shrines or pavilions within temple complexes.
 
• They may serve various purposes, such as housing subsidiary deities or providing space for specific rituals.
